# sca init

[← Command reference](../commands.md)

`<sca_options>` are the [global options](../commands.md#global-options).

```text
The initialize command help

The initialize command is used for initializing a security related system - a
storage or device.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] init [<init_options>] <system>

init_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help

allowed values for the system are:

  - yubikey        - initialize yubikey hardware security module - first time
                     initialization
  - openssl_ca_db  - initialize OpenSSL database
  - sca_usb_stick  - initalize sca usb stick
  - demo           - initialize demo certificate authority
```

**See also**

```text
Run 'sca init <system> -h' for getting help specific to a the given system
initialization.
```

**Subcommands**

- [demo](#sca-init-demo) - initialize demo certificate authority
- [openssl_ca_db](#sca-init-openssl_ca_db) - initialize OpenSSL database
- [sca_usb_stick](#sca-init-sca_usb_stick) - initalize sca usb stick
- [yubikey](#sca-init-yubikey) - initialize yubikey hardware security module - first time initialization

## sca init demo

```text
The initialize demo command help

The initialize demo command is used for initializing a demo ca consisting of all
the directories and files to reflect a fully setup use-case with two CAs, and
one of them with subca's user's host's and service's defined.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] init [<init_options>] demo <demo_options> [<demo_folder>]

init_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help

demo_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help

The demo_folder is the root folder in which to initialize the demo.
The default for demo_folder is ~/.sca/demo/ (the demo_folder_default
setting).
```

**What it creates:**
- Root CA (key + self-signed certificate)
- Sub-CA (key + certificate signed by root)
- Sample service certificate
- Sample user certificate

**Example:**
```bash
# Create demo in default location (~/.sca/demo/)
sca init demo

# Create demo in custom location
sca init demo /tmp/sca-demo
```

This is useful for:
- Learning how sca works
- Testing certificate workflows
- Development and debugging

## sca init openssl_ca_db

```text
The initialize OpenSSL Certificate Authority Database command help

The initialize OpenSSL Certificate Authority Database command is used for
initializing a OpenSSL ca directories and files required for it to properly
function.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] init [<init_options>] openssl_ca_db <openssl_ca_db_options> <entity>

init_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help

openssl_ca_db_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help

allowed values for the entity are:

  - ca            - for current certificate authority
  - subca         - for current sub-ordinate certificate authority
  - user          - for current user (not recommended to use)
  - host          - for current host (not recommended to use)
  - service       - for current service (not recommended to use)
```

Creates the `index.txt` and `serial` files required by OpenSSL for tracking issued certificates.

## sca init sca_usb_stick

```text
The initialize sca USB stick command help

The initialize sca USB stick command is used for initializing USB stick
used for booting into secure offline environment with sca and it's prerequisites
already available.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] init [<init_options>] sca_usb_stick <sca_usb_stick_options> [<ubuntu_version_id>]

init_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help

sca_usb_stick_options:

  -h, --help                    - print this help
  -s, --skip-cleanup            - optional flag, preserve intermediary files
                                  created during live iso image creation.
                                  this option is useful in case you want to
                                  further customize sca iso image.
  -t, --test-image              - optional flag create iso image for sca test.
                                  the slight
                                  difference between the regular image is that
                                  the test image automatically starts sca test
                                  on login, writes the results to the disk
                                  labelled sca-test-results and shuts down.
                                  without such a disk it runs no tests and
                                  touches no disk.
  -i, --include-apt-mirror      - optional flag includes the ubuntu main and
                                  restricted repositories within the image by
                                  storing apt-mirror within it and configuring
                                  offline environment package manager to use it.
                                  NOTE: the packages sca needs are bundled
                                  regardless of this option, see -y and -x.
  -y, --yubikey-support         - optional flag bundles the yubikey tools in
                                  the image and installs them along with sca:
                                  ykcs11, yubico-piv-tool, yubikey-manager
                                  (ykman), gnupg and scdaemon.
  -x, --exclude-pkcs11-support  - optional flag if specified excludes bundling of pkcs11
                                  support in the generated sca usb image:
                                  pcscd, libccid, opensc, opensc-pkcs11,
                                  libengine-pkcs11-openssl and pkcs11-provider.
  -o, --no-cache-iso            - optional flag indicating we do not want to
                                  preserve a copy of the downloaded iso file
                                  for the specified ubuntu_version_id.
                                  default value is false.
                                  default behavior is to cache the iso file
                                  per ubuntu_version_id in the ~/.sca/downloads/
                                  folder, and to reuse it in the next runs once
                                  it matches the published SHA256SUMS.
  -n, --no-cache                - optional flag.
                                  default value is false.
                                  switches off all caching. suitable for one
                                  time runs, where there is no advantage in
                                  caching large downloaded files. same as
                                  --no-cache-iso.

The <ubuntu_version_id> parameter is optional. The only supported, and default,
ubuntu version id is 26.04-resolute. Its form is "<major>.<minor>-<release_name>".
The latest point release of this version is downloaded and checked against the
published SHA256SUMS. Any other ubuntu version id is rejected.

The sca usb stick image is built on, and only on, an ubuntu host of the same
version, 26.04-resolute. On any other host the command fails before
downloading anything.

The sca iso image is written to ~/.sca/downloads/ next to the original ubuntu
iso, together with a <image>.options file recording the -y, -i and -x options
it was built with. If the image already exists, it is reused only when those
recorded options match the ones requested. Otherwise - including an image built
before sca recorded its options - the command fails, printing the options the
image has and the ones requested, and leaves the image alone. Remove the image
and its options file to build a new one. A test image (-t) is always rebuilt.
```

Creates a bootable Ubuntu live USB with sca pre-installed for air-gapped root CA operations.

**Ubuntu version:** `26.04-resolute` only (the default). The image is built on an
Ubuntu 26.04 host only; any other version id or host fails with an error. The
stick bundles OpenSSL 3.5, pkcs11-provider 1.2, OpenSC 0.27, pcscd/libccid,
yubico-piv-tool and ykcs11 2.7, yubikey-manager 5.8, and GnuPG with scdaemon
2.4, all from the Ubuntu 26.04 archive. See
[Tools on the stick](../air-gapped-operations.md#tools-on-the-stick).

**Reusing a built image:** an existing image is reused only if its
`<image>.options` file matches the `-y`, `-i` and `-x` options requested;
otherwise the command fails (see the syntax above). To build a new one, remove
both files:

```bash
rm -f ~/.sca/downloads/ubuntu-26.04.1-desktop-amd64.sca.iso{,.options}
```

**Example:**

```bash
# Create USB image with YubiKey support
sca init sca_usb_stick --yubikey-support

# Write to USB (replace sdX with your device)
sudo dd bs=4M if=~/.sca/downloads/ubuntu-26.04.1-desktop-amd64.sca.iso of=/dev/sdX conv=fdatasync
```

See [Air-Gapped Operations](../air-gapped-operations.md) for complete workflow documentation.

## sca init yubikey

```text
The initialize yubikey command help

The initialize yubikey command is used for initializing a security hardware device
from Yubico company called yubikey.

The initialization is necessary only in first time use of the key in case it was
previously uninitialized. The key comes pre-initialized with publicly known
credentials and therefore needs re-creating of all it's access keys:
  - management key
  - pin key
  - puk key

Those are automatically changed from default factory preset to randomly generated
and saved values.

It is recommended to issue init command every now and then with --roll-keys option
so that you refresh the stale access passwords for a yubikey.

IMPORTANT: In case you have already initialized yubikey, you will need to
configure the above mentioned keys by setting the content of the related entity
hw key configuration settings.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] init [<init_options>] yubikey <yubikey_options>

init_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help

yubikey_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help
  -r, --roll-keys - roll yubikey management key, pin and puk by changing the old
                    values with newly randomized ones
```

**See also**

```text
See yubico web site for more information on their products.
```

See also [`sca security_key init`](security_key.md#sca-security_key-init), which also supports `--device`.
